chapter_title: Concerning the Summons, in which Limb of the Soul
spiritual_reading:
The primal good that should have held all things together poured itself outward and became scattered, and the living consciousness that depended on its unity was torn into separated powers, so that it no longer recognized what it had been given to know. Yet the blessed and glorious Divine-Human approached in an unperceived way, and entered that state by the likeness of His own order, by the form of His own life, by the warmth of His own love, and by pure wisdom itself, which is the illumination of truth from the Divine.

Just as in the outward person the governing principle holds all subordinate functions in connection, so in the inner person every operative power depends on the supreme of order. If some subordinate power is injured or removed while the governing principle remains, restoration is still possible; but if the governing principle itself is rejected and severed, the whole organized life of that person perishes, and the state is lost.

So it was in that first spiritual state: the governing good was as the ruling principle, and the derivative powers were the subordinate functions of its life that were meant to remain conjoined to it. And conversely, it was also like the general influx that gives vitality to every part in the outermost degree, by which all things there receive their activity and continuance. This ruling principle was held in the highest degree of the spiritual order, supported in its connection with the ultimate foundation of heaven by the Divine presence that sustains what is below.

So too with the Father, the blessed Divine-Human: He is the supreme from which all organization proceeds, and He is the general influx that keeps all things in being; and He is set in the highest degree upon the ultimate foundation of heaven, made steadfast by pure wisdom that is from Him and is His living consciousness, with which He invests Himself for operation.

From Himself He brought forth and sent out the sufficient powers by which His purpose is accomplished in lower degrees: the faculty that receives and arranges, the faculty that thinks and forms, the faculty that sees inwardly, the faculty that provides order for action, and the faculty that weighs and judges. He followed after them by continual influx, because what belongs to His living consciousness was entangled among those who resist order; for those entangled powers were like the subordinate functions of that life, bound within the ultimate domain of the spiritual world.

When those powers had gone forth, He remained conjoined with pure wisdom, and from that union He rose into active intercession, asking and imploring that the needed strength be granted. Then the Divine granted tranquility and conjunction, and gave the certainty of deliverance and restoration of the Divine-Human in that scattered state. And the Divine-Human from this received what was required for the work: He restored the separated powers, gathered the dispersed consciousness back into order, and established it in its proper degree as a fixed structure of conjunction.

He then brought that restored consciousness into a determinate form and perfected it with skill, arranging it according to the order of heaven; and He sent forth living utterances of truth so that they might descend into the obscurity, extinguish what was inflamed by opposition, and raise up the consciousness that had been crushed by evil. Those scattered powers were gathered back within; they returned and were made steadfast again, reformed into the likeness of their Divine source.

fills.notes: The substrate describes the First Man’s self-diffusion: the ruling good going outward into ultimates, causing dispersion of the soul’s powers. This matches the spiritual sense: “poured itself outward and became scattered.”
Requires a distributive term before “limb of the living soul,” since the sense is that every derivative power was dispersed.
Balances the parallelism: “limb … of the living soul … of the living soul.” The teaching layer regularly alternates “limb” and “member” for derivative powers.
Spiritual sense: the scattered state “no longer recognized what it had been given to know.” Old layer frames this as loss of self-recognition in dispersion.
In the body analogy: if a limb is cut off while the head remains, there is hope of restoration. “Healing” best fits the impersonal, structural register (not moral exhortation).
Living air correspondence = general influx giving vitality as one breathes and is sustained in it. The missing verb must express continuance-in-being by influx.
He is “set … upon the Pillar” in the highest degree. The lacuna after “set i[n ...]” demands a locative expressing the supreme placement above the ultimate foundation.
The Father “clothes” himself with his Light-Virgin (pure wisdom as living consciousness) for operation. The instrumental phrase is required by the correspondential sense of investiture.
Introduces the list of sent powers as an emanation from the Father. This matches the spiritual sense: “From Himself He brought forth and sent out the sufficient powers.”
The demonstrative “those …” needs its noun: the produced faculties/powers listed next.
He follows behind them by continual influx “for the sake of his living soul” (i.e., because it is entangled). This is the causal connector required by the spiritual logic.

fills.notes: The entangled powers are “like the limbs of its body” and are bound within the ultimate domain. The phrase supplies the required binding-into-ultimates relation before “universe.”
The giver of peace and kiss is the transcendent source (the Father). In the oldest layer this remains impersonal-cosmological: the supreme grants conjunction and calm to the operative Divine-Man.
The kiss corresponds to conjunction/union; specifying “of peace” matches the immediately preceding “he gave him peace,” keeping the old layer’s structural pairing.
What is announced is not moral ‘gospel’ but certainty of deliverance: good tidings about restoration. This aligns with the spiritual translation’s “certainty of deliverance and restoration.”
After receiving peace and assurance, the Man receives the operative power needed: to restore limbs and gather the dispersed soul. This bridges to “his limbs and gathered his soul …”.
The gathering results in re-establishment in the proper degree/location, matching “he built it in its place like this tower.”
The “tower” image corresponds to a fixed structure of conjunction in higher order; specifying “of the heights” keeps the cosmological register and links to placement on the Pillar.
Resumes the acting subject (the restored Divine-Man) continuing the forming and beautifying work.
Maintains verbal sequence: “Then he … shaped it and beautified it …”.
After “form” the text requires an ordering principle: arranging the restored soul “according to” the heavenly pattern, matching the spiritual sense “according to the order of heaven.”
Introduces purpose clause for the sent “voices” (living utterances) to descend and effect quenching and raising.
The inflamed opposition to be quenched corresponds, in the old cosmological register, to a ‘fire’ state in the rebels. “Wrath” preserves impersonal passion-state rather than moral sermonizing.

assessment: Most lacunae here are tightly constrained by the chapter’s correspondential anatomy: head and limbs (governing good and derivative powers), living air (general influx), Pillar of Glory (ultimate foundation supporting higher degrees), and the Light-Virgin (pure wisdom as living consciousness/investiture). Single-letter brackets are certain. Larger gaps are recoverable in direction and function (dispersion, loss of recognition, emanated powers, conjunction as peace and kiss, restoration as building a tower, utterances quenching the rebels’ fire), though exact phrasing remains occasionally approximate where the Coptic base could allow several near-synonyms.
